events.title: Preliminary Peace Signed Ending the American Revolution
events.description: In Paris, American and British representatives signed preliminary peace articles. These terms settled the main questions between the two sides after years of war. They were later formalized in the 1783 Treaty of Paris.
events.significance: Britain's recognition of American independence was the diplomatic turning point of the Revolutionary War. It set the borders and terms of the new United States.

events.title: Mark Twain Is Born
events.description: Samuel Langhorne Clemens was born in Florida, Missouri. He wrote under the pen name Mark Twain. His books include The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and Adventures of Huckleberry Finn.
events.significance: Twain's humor and his accounts of American life made him one of the country's best-loved authors. Many critics regard Huckleberry Finn as a landmark of American literature.

events.title: Winston Churchill Is Born at Blenheim Palace
events.description: The future British statesman, orator and author was born at Blenheim Palace in England. He went on to serve twice as prime minister, from 1940 to 1945 and from 1951 to 1955.
events.significance: Churchill's leadership and speeches rallied Britain during World War II. He remains one of the most influential figures of the 20th century.

events.title: The Soviet Union Invades Finland
events.description: Soviet forces attacked Finland with a very large force and bombed Helsinki. This began the Winter War. Finland had refused Soviet demands for a naval base and other concessions.
events.significance: Finland's resistance against far larger forces drew international admiration. The invasion also led to the Soviet Union's expulsion from the League of Nations.
